title: First Absent Multiple of K
statement:
You get an array nums of positive integers and a positive integer k.

Return the smallest positive multiple of k (that is k, 2k, 3k, …) that does not appear in nums.

examples.why: 3, 6 and 9 are all present, so the first gap is 12. The 4 is not a multiple of 3 and does not matter.
The gap is in the middle. Returning max + k (10) would skip it.
Every positive integer is a multiple of 1, and 1 is missing.

hints: Try k, 2k, 3k, … in order. The question for each candidate is only: is it in nums?
Membership checks in a plain array cost O(n) each. How do you make them O(1)?
Put nums in a hash set. There are only n values, so at most n + 1 candidates are checked before a gap appears.

explain.intuition:
The answer is the first multiple in the sequence k, 2k, 3k, … that is missing, so you walk that sequence and check each candidate. The array holds only n values, so at most n multiples can be present and the walk stops within n + 1 steps.

What makes it fast is the membership check. Scanning the array for each candidate is O(n) per check and O(n²) overall. A hash set turns each check into O(1), the same way you would keep a Set of selected ids instead of searching an array on every render.
steps: Put every value of nums into a set.
While m is in the set, add k to m.
pitfalls: Returning the largest multiple present plus k. A gap in the middle is the answer, as in [2, 4, 8].
Starting at 0. Zero is a multiple of every k, but the task asks for a positive one.
Checking membership with includes or in list inside the loop, which is O(n²) when the array holds k, 2k, …, nk.

solutions.title: Linear search per candidate
solutions.idea: Walk k, 2k, 3k, … and scan the array for each candidate.

solutions.title: Hash set
solutions.idea: Same walk, but membership is an O(1) set lookup. At most n + 1 candidates are checked.

followups: Solve it in O(1) extra space if you may reorder nums. (Hint: place each value v = j·k with j ≤ n at index j − 1.)
Answer many queries with different k on the same array. What would you precompute?
